title: Inverse Johnson transformation (convert back to non-transformed value)
label2: Select a variable or type in a numeric value to be converted back from a prior Johnson transformation
variableSelcted: Select a variable (also used to read the stored Johnson parameters unless manually specified below)
selectVariableRad: Option 1: Select a variable to be converted back from a prior Johnson transformation
invJohnsonColName: (Optional) Specify a new variable name to store the converted values. Otherwise <variable_invjtrans> will be created
selectNumberRad: Option 2: Type in a numeric value to be converted back from a Johnson transformation
manualParamsChk: Manually specify the Johnson transformation type and parameters below. Otherwise, if unchecked, the type and parameters stored with the variable selected above (by a prior Johnson transformation) will be used
lambda: Lambda (λ) - must be greater than 0 for SB and SU. May be left blank for SL (not used, defaults to 1)
digits: Digits - rounds to the specified number of decimal places

help.title: Transform back (inverse) from a prior Johnson transformed value
help.body:
Description
Transform back (inverse) from a prior Johnson transformed value using the transformation type (SB, SL, or SU) and the parameters Gamma (γ), Eta (η), Epsilon (ε), Lambda (λ)

The type and parameters are read from the attributes stored with the selected variable by the companion Johnson transformation dialog (jtrans_type, jtrans_gamma, jtrans_eta, jtrans_epsilon, jtrans_lambda), or they can be manually specified - for example, to invert a transformation that was performed in Minitab, whose output reports these same parameters

The three Johnson transformation functions and their inverses
SB (bounded): Y = γ + η * Ln( (X - ε) / (λ + ε - X) )
inverse: X = ε + λ / ( 1 + Exp( -( Y - γ ) / η ) )

SL (lognormal): Y = γ + η * Ln( X - ε )
inverse: X = ε + Exp( ( Y - γ ) / η )

SU (unbounded): Y = γ + η * Asinh( (X - ε) / λ )
inverse: X = ε + λ * Sinh( ( Y - γ ) / η )

Note: the inverse recovers the original values up to the rounding that was applied when the transformed values were stored
